acceptance: morize-core exports UnixTimestamp and TimestampError from one new timestamp module, with no additional clock, calendar, serialization, or domain behavior.
UnixTimestamp::new accepts nanoseconds 0 and 999_999_999 and rejects 1_000_000_000 with TimestampError::NanosecondsOutOfRange carrying only the rejected numeric nanosecond value.
UnixTimestamp::from_seconds(0) represents the Unix epoch exactly and returns seconds=0 and nanoseconds=0.

The instant one-half second before the epoch is represented as seconds=-1 and nanoseconds=500_000_000 and sorts before the epoch; seconds=-1,nanoseconds=999_999_999 sorts immediately before the epoch.
Valid timestamps with i64::MIN and i64::MAX seconds are accepted when nanoseconds are normalized; this Grain performs no arithmetic that can overflow those boundaries.
Equality, ordering, and hashing are deterministic over the normalized (seconds, nanoseconds) pair, and derived ordering matches chronological ordering under the invariant.
TimestampError Display/Debug are bounded numeric diagnostics and contain no calendar/timezone inference or executable semantics.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes and includes focused normalization, pre-epoch, boundary, ordering, and error tests.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; the Grain admits no runtime, build, or test dependency.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.

An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for normalization correctness, pre-epoch semantics, boundary behavior, deterministic ordering, scope containment, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisite for SG-000011 revalidates against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.
The implementation changes no path outside crates/morize-core/src/timestamp.rs and crates/morize-core/src/lib.rs.

method.control: Implementation is limited to one dependency-free timestamp value/error module, focused tests, and morize-core re-exports. No system clock, arithmetic, calendar/timezone conversion, parsing/formatting, serde, persistence, domain timestamps, or third-party dependency is authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head, normalized nanosecond invariant, pre-epoch ordering semantics, boundary behavior, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the timestamp primitive implementation commits; no persisted format, migration, or user data depends on this Grain.

minimality.rationale: A two-field standard-library-only Unix timestamp value is the smallest precise in-memory time primitive that supports pre-epoch and subsecond ordering without choosing text formats, timezones, clocks, persistence schemas, or third-party libraries.

outcome: morize-core exposes a dependency-free UnixTimestamp value as signed whole seconds from the Unix epoch plus a normalized nanosecond fraction, with deterministic ordering and validation but no calendar, timezone, parsing, formatting, clock, or persistence behavior.
rationale: P1 explicitly requires timestamps and DATA_MODEL requires an exact timestamp representation. A seconds-plus-nanoseconds value preserves subsecond precision without narrowing the usable i64 second range, while keeping text/wire formats, clocks, timezone conversion, leap-second policy, and domain semantics separate.

risk.recovery: Revert the timestamp primitive implementation commits; no persistent format or user data has been written by this Grain.

scope_in: Define public UnixTimestamp with private seconds: i64 and nanoseconds: u32 fields; seconds are signed whole seconds relative to 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and nanoseconds are the fractional part within that second.
Require the normalized invariant 0 <= nanoseconds < 1_000_000_000; reject any larger nanosecond value with bounded TimestampError::NanosecondsOutOfRange { nanoseconds }.
Define pre-epoch semantics explicitly: negative instants use floor-style whole seconds plus a non-negative fraction, so -0.5 seconds is represented as seconds=-1, nanoseconds=500_000_000.
Provide checked new(seconds, nanoseconds), from_seconds(seconds), seconds(), nanoseconds(), is_before_epoch(), and deterministic Copy/Clone/Eq/Ord/Hash value semantics.

Add standard-library-only tests for epoch, positive and negative instants, the -0.5-second representation, nanosecond boundaries, i64::MIN/i64::MAX seconds, chronological ordering, and bounded error diagnostics.
scope_out: SystemTime/clock reads, current-time helpers, duration arithmetic, addition/subtraction, overflow policy for arithmetic, monotonic time, sequence ordering, or scheduler behavior.
RFC3339/ISO-8601 or other text parsing/formatting, timezone/calendar conversion, daylight-saving behavior, explicit leap-second representation, locale behavior, or human display policy.

Serde or other serialization-framework integration, persisted/wire schemas, configuration formats, migrations, database mapping, domain record timestamps, policy, storage, retrieval, MCP, models, or any third-party dependency.
title: Add normalized Unix timestamp primitive
